newsitem.title: SIERRA LEONE: Sierra Leone foreign minister defects - officials.
newsitem.headline: Sierra Leone foreign minister defects - officials.

text.p: The foreign minister of Sierra Leone's military junta has defected after leading a delegation to failed peace talks in Ivory Coast, officials said on Monday.

A United Nations official in neighbouring Guinea told Reuters Pallo Bangura was still in the Ivorian city of Abidjan where the talks collapsed last Friday. But one official source in Freetown said he had since gone on to Addis Ababa, Ethiopia.
"Pallo Bangura, the Sierra Leone foreign minister, defected from the Sierra Leone delegation in Abidjan and is still in Abidjan," the U.N. official said by phone from Conakry.
There was speculation in Freetown that other members of the Abidjan team had defected. They named former ambassador Dauda Kamara, said to have applied for political asylum in Britain.

A junta official said: "We have heard that some members of the delegation we sent to Abidjan have defected, but we don't know for sure. We are waiting for the delegation to come back, which they are supposed to do today."
Diplomats in Abidjan said Bangura and Kamara did not show up at the airport when the rest of the 20-man team flew back home.
Junta officials were in Abidjan last week for talks with West African foreign ministers on resolving the crisis in Sierra Leone since the military took power on May 25.
West African ECOMOG troops, led by Nigeria, have imposed an air, sea and land blockade in an attempt to restore ousted civilian president Ahmad Tejan Kabbah.
The talks broke down on July 30 when junta leader Johnny Paul Koroma said the military would stay in power until 2001.
